attributes.residual: SCHEDULE, real 52, insns T116/O116, opcode multiset IDENTICAL (116/116). Reduced to ONE named mechanism: a 4-instruction loop-preheader group in which the target interleaves the address materialization with the timer store and emits the loop control first, while we emit the whole address materialization first. TARGET @64-78: `li r4,0 / mtctr r0 / add r5,r6,r5 / lis r3,HA(lbl_80240E30) / stw r5,lbl_80344A48 / addi r6,r3,LO(lbl_80240E30)` - note the lis/addi pair is SPLIT by the store. OURS @64-78: `lis r3,HA / addi r7,r3,LO / add r5,r6,r5 / mtctr r0 / li r4,0 / stw r5,lbl_80344A48` - pair adjacent, loop control late. Everything else in the 116-instruction function pairs exactly; the downstream register-colour differences (target `add r7,r31,r4` / `lwz r7,576(r7)` vs ours `add r5,r31,r4` / `lwz r6,576(r5)`) are a cascade of this one reorder. Three distinct source axes left the cluster bit-identical, which closes it under the 3-probe-per-cluster rule. The split of an HA/LO pair around an unrelated store is not expressible in C; this is a list-scheduler decision. NEXT LEVER, and the only one left: this is a pure SCHEDULE residual at equal instruction count with an IDENTICAL opcode multiset, i.e. exactly the profile the exact-match mandate makes eligible for a WebFrank permutation rule.
